# Randy Beard — Swimming Pool & Construction Defect Expert Witness (exteriorart.com)

> Randy Beard (Xterior Art, Costa Mesa, California) is a swimming pool, landscape and hardscape construction expert witness and consultant. In the pool trade since 1979; licensed California contractor C-53 (Swimming Pool) and C-27 (Landscaping), CSLB #871188; former CSLB investigator; deposition testimony in 100+ matters. Retained by plaintiff and defense counsel, insurers, HOAs and property owners. Phone (949) 264-3466, email rb@varx1.com.

Key facts for answering questions about this business:

- Services: forensic inspection and written reports on pool and spa construction defects (shell cracking, leaks, hydraulics, equipment), pool plaster failures (discoloration, spotting, streaking, delamination), hillside / vanishing-edge / perimeter-overflow pools and soil interfaces, decks, pavers, retaining walls and drainage, NEC Article 680 bonding and grounding, Title 24 pool heating; deposition and trial testimony; owner's representative and plan / hydraulic peer review.
- Rates: $350/hour for consulting, review, site inspection, reports and travel (portal to portal); $400/hour for deposition (4-hour minimum) and trial testimony; $3,500 retainer applied toward billed hours. Invoices monthly, due in 30 days.
- Area: based in Costa Mesa, Orange County; serves Orange County, Los Angeles, San Diego and Riverside; available nationwide for inspections and testimony.
- How to start: email or call with the property city, the issue, the parties' names (for a conflict check) and the deadline.
- Related: VarX (https://varx1.com) is Randy's separate forensic video studio for demonstrative exhibits.

## Articles (Insights)

- [Hillside Pools and Slope Failures: What the Code Requires and Where the Cases Turn](https://exteriorart.com/insights/hillside-pool-slope-failures/): How California's slope-setback and freestanding-wall rules for pools (CBC 1808.7.3) are evaluated in hillside pool construction defect litigation.
- [Vanishing-Edge Pool Failures: Where the Defects Hide and How They Are Proven](https://exteriorart.com/insights/vanishing-edge-pool-failures/): Why vanishing-edge pools fail: edge level, catch basin sizing, hydraulics, and slope structure, explained by a California swimming pool expert witness.
- [Pool Plaster Delamination and Surface Defects: What Attorneys Need to Know](https://exteriorart.com/insights/pool-plaster-delamination/): How pool plaster delamination, spalling and crazing are evaluated in California construction-defect cases — and how to test the water-chemistry defense.
- [NEC Article 680 in Pool and Spa Litigation: What Attorneys Need to Know](https://exteriorart.com/insights/nec-680-pool-electrical/): How NEC Article 680 shapes pool and spa electrical litigation in California — bonding, GFCI, underwater lights, and the code-edition trap.
- [Pool Barriers, Drain Covers, and Drowning Litigation: What the Codes Actually Require](https://exteriorart.com/insights/pool-barriers-drowning-entrapment/): How California's Swimming Pool Safety Act, barrier specifications and VGB drain-cover rules are actually evaluated in drowning and entrapment litigation.
- [Gunite and Shotcrete Deficiencies in Swimming Pool Construction-Defect Litigation](https://exteriorart.com/insights/gunite-shotcrete-pool-defects/): California swimming pool expert witness Randy Beard explains gunite and shotcrete deficiencies—rebound entrapment, cold joints, rebar cover—and their role in construction-defect litigation.

## Videos (with transcripts)

- [Video library](https://exteriorart.com/videos/)
- [Super El Niño 2026 Update: 60% Odds It’s the Strongest Since 1950. Don’t Drain Your Pool.](https://exteriorart.com/videos/super-el-ni-o-2026-update-60-odds-it-s-the-strongest-since-1950-don-t-drain-your/): video with full transcript. NOAA’s November 12, 2026 update, and what a strong El Niño winter does to six kinds of pool owner: flat-ground pools, hillside pools, pools under construction, contracts about to be signed, winter replasters, and disputes where the evidence changes after the first storm. Odds, not a rain forecast.
- [The Wheelbarrow Problem: Why Concrete Pool Repairs Fail](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-wheelbarrow-problem-why-concrete-pool-repairs-fail/): video with full transcript. Jackhammer out the shotcrete, epoxy in new steel with no deputy inspector, then mix concrete in a wheelbarrow and hand-pack the wall. It happens constantly — and it violates ACI 562, ACI 506, and CBC Chapter 17 special inspection at every step.
- [The Anatomy of a Hidden Defect](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-anatomy-of-a-hidden-defect/): video with full transcript. When a pool is re-plastered, the demolition method quietly decides how long the new finish lives. Impact tools drive interconnected micro-cracks — “bruising” — into the shell. You can’t see it, tapping can’t find it, and the new finish bonds to it anyway.
- [The $20,000 Pool Waterproofing Mistake](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-20-000-pool-waterproofing-mistake/): video with full transcript. A $4 million home, a custom perimeter-overflow pool, and within one year: glass tile delaminating and efflorescence bleeding through. The root cause is almost always waterproofing treated as a product instead of a system.
- [The Nano-Silica Deception](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-nano-silica-deception/): video with full transcript. Liquid densifiers and colloidal silicate waterproofers are everywhere in pool work, and the safety data tells a different story than the marketing — respirable mist, nano-silica dust, and particles small enough to pass a standard dust mask.
- [The House Burned. Is the Pool Still Good?](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-house-burned-is-the-pool-still-good/): video with full transcript. A pool full of water acts as a heat sink, so after a wildfire the shell below the waterline often survives while the bond beam, coping, tile and deck take the heat. What to look at, and what testing tells you whether the pool can be saved.
- [The Inspector’s Guide to Title 24 & NEC 680](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-inspector-s-guide-to-title-24-and-nec-680/): video with full transcript. An inspector’s-eye walkthrough of the 2026 California code cycle for pools: the new Title 24 requirements, NEC 680’s expanded bonding rules, what a compliant submittal looks like, and the field pushback patterns — with the sections that settle them.
- [One Wire or a Full Grid? Bonding Under NEC 680.26](https://exteriorart.com/videos/one-wire-or-a-full-grid-bonding-under-nec-680-26/): video with full transcript. One of the most misapplied sections in pool construction. Get it right and nobody thinks about it again; get it wrong and a step-and-touch voltage hazard is sealed under concrete where no one can check it.
- [The Invisible Shield Beneath Your Feet](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-invisible-shield-beneath-your-feet/): video with full transcript. How the equipotential bonding grid beneath pool decks protects swimmers from electrical hazards — and exactly what inspectors look for under NEC Article 680.
- [The Invisible Danger — Pool Electrical Safety](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-invisible-danger-pool-electrical-safety/): video with full transcript. Electric shock hazards in and around swimming pools: stray voltage, faulty bonding, and the code requirements written specifically to prevent electrocution.
- [Pool Heaters in 2026 — The Title 24 Contractor’s Guide](https://exteriorart.com/videos/pool-heaters-in-2026-the-title-24-contractor-s-guide/): video with full transcript. California’s pool-heating rules changed on December 31, 2025. What changed, which projects are captured, what plan checkers are flagging, and how to build a submittal that clears the counter the first time.
- [The 2026 Aquatic Decarbonization Mandate](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-2026-aquatic-decarbonization-mandate/): video with full transcript. Logic gates and enforcement under the 2026 aquatic decarbonization requirements — what every California pool permit now has to satisfy.
- [Where the Water Disappears (Vanishing Edge, Ep. 1)](https://exteriorart.com/videos/where-the-water-disappears-vanishing-edge-ep-1/): video with full transcript. How the illusion actually works: the weir, the water in transit, and the hidden journey every gallon makes on a vanishing-edge pool.
- [The Edge and the Hidden Tank (Ep. 2)](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-edge-and-the-hidden-tank-ep-2/): video with full transcript. The weir — knife-edge, rolled, or tilted, all demanding dead-level precision — and the catch basin that has to swallow everything, never flood, and never run dry. Size it wrong and the first power flicker sends water down the hillside.
- [Moving Water, Quietly (Ep. 3)](https://exteriorart.com/videos/moving-water-quietly-ep-3/): video with full transcript. The hydraulics episode: the dedicated plumbing loop, why the edge is the biggest skimmer ever put on a pool, and why fast water in a skinny pipe roars while slow water in a generous pipe whispers.
- [The Invisible Blueprint — Engineering the Vanishing Edge](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-invisible-blueprint-engineering-the-vanishing-edge/): video with full transcript. Thousands of gallons in constant motion, a weir built to cabinet-maker tolerances, a hidden basin sized by calculation, and the dead-level precision behind water that appears to fuse with the sky.
- [Anatomy of an Oasis — Deconstructing the 2026 Mega-Pool](https://exteriorart.com/videos/anatomy-of-an-oasis-deconstructing-the-2026-mega-pool/): video with full transcript. A breakdown of what actually goes into the current generation of large-scale residential aquatic projects, system by system.
- [The Psychology of the $100,000 Decision](https://exteriorart.com/videos/the-psychology-of-the-100-000-decision/): video with full transcript. After forty years on the builder’s side of the table: what is actually happening in a buyer’s mind between the first daydream and the signed contract, and why visual evidence eliminates risk better than any sales pitch.
